h1: Makathanee Resort — the Ao Kao beachfront resort where the boat docks at your doorstep
intro: What sets Makathanee Resort apart from other stays on Koh Mak is simple: speedboats from the mainland, Koh Chang and Koh Kood dock at the resort's own pier — it's under 100 metres from boat to check-in desk. This Ao Kao beachfront resort began as just 8 beach bungalows and grew into a full property with two pools and a wide range of rooms, from beachfront bungalows to family suites. From approx. ฿1,400/night, breakfast included.

body.html: Makathanee is one of Koh Mak's pioneer resorts. It started life as just 8 beach bungalows on Ao Kao Beach and gradually expanded into a full property with a hotel block, two pools and rooms across several price tiers. The advantage guests mention most is that the resort has its own pier — speedboats from Laem Ngop, Koh Chang and Koh Kood moor right here, and it's under 100 metres from the boat to the lobby. No need to wait for a shared songthaew into the resort the way you do at many places on the island.

Ao Kao Beach runs along the southern side of the island: white sand and rows of coconut palms the length of the shore. In front of the resort the water shelves in gently, which makes it easy for kids to paddle in the shallows. There are two outdoor pools set in tropical gardens — one with bubble-jet seating — and in the evening the beachfront restaurant and a sand-level night BBQ with a cocktail bar open up. It's a favourite spot for guests to sit and catch the sea breeze.
"The boat pulls right up in front of the hotel — you just wheel your bag a few steps into your room. So easy. In the evening we had the beach BBQ listening to the waves; lovely atmosphere."

There really is a wide choice of rooms: budget-friendly Standard City View, pool- and sea-view rooms in two-storey blocks, beach bungalows that open onto a lawn running down to the sand, Deluxe rooms, Honeymoon Suites with in-room jacuzzis, and two-bedroom Family Suites with a living area. Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, TV, hot water, a safe and tea/coffee facilities. The renovated rooms in the newer hotel block earn praise for being clean and spacious, while the older bungalows have beachfront charm but some are showing their age.

Honestly, from the reviews: the most common complaint is upkeep and consistency between rooms. Some guests note the buildings and certain rooms feel run down and tired, and that staff training and cleanliness aren't always uniform. The other thing to know is that the beach on this side can get very shallow at low tide, with patches of seagrass — a few visitors feel the sand here isn't as nice as on the Ao Suan Yai side. Even so, many feel the beachfront location, the private pier and the approachable prices keep the overall value high.

What guests consistently praise is friendly, welcoming staff, tasty Thai food at the beachfront restaurant, and breakfast included in the room rate. The resort also has a mini-mart, a tour desk and rentals for motorbikes and golf carts, and can arrange diving, fishing and island tours — all in one place. It suits travellers who want a beachfront resort that's easy to reach and isn't chasing luxury, just an easygoing slice of Koh Mak at a friendly price.

The bottom line from real reviews: Makathanee is a sensible pick for families and anyone who values convenience — boat at the door, on the beach, two pools, rooms in many shapes and prices. From around ฿1,400/night for a pool-view or Deluxe room in normal season, rising in high season, with beach bungalows and suites around ฿2,000–3,800. It scores around 8.3 from real guests. If you can accept that some rooms are dated and the beach here is shallow at low tide, the location and value here are hard to find elsewhere on the island.

honestSummary: Makathanee is a beachfront resort that sells convenience and value above all — boat at the door, on the beach, two pools, rooms in many shapes and prices, great for families. The trade-off is that some rooms are dated and cleanliness isn't uniform everywhere; if you can accept that, the location and pricing here are hard to find elsewhere on Koh Mak.
honestChecks: If you expect flawless, brand-new rooms — the older bungalows and some rooms feel tired → ask for a renovated room in the hotel block, or the Deluxe/Suite tier, when you book.

If a beautiful deep-water beach is your top priority — Ao Kao here gets very shallow at low tide with seagrass → time it with high tide, or choose the Ao Suan Yai side if you want sunset views and clear water.
If you're going in low season (Jun–mid-Oct) — many places on Koh Mak close and the sea can be rough on some days → confirm with the resort that it's open and that boats are running before you book.

tips.title: Make the most of the resort's pier
tips.body: Tell the resort which mainland pier you're coming from. Many speedboats dock at Makathanee's own pier, so you walk straight in — saving the songthaew fare.

tips.title: Ask for the new block if cleanliness matters
tips.body: Deluxe/Suite rooms in the hotel block are newer than the older bungalows. Specify this at booking to get a room in better condition.

tips.title: Check the tide times
tips.body: Ao Kao in front of the resort gets very shallow at low tide. If you want to swim in deeper water, check the tide chart before heading down.

tips.title: Bring your own mosquito repellent
tips.body: Koh Mak is a natural island and there are mosquitoes in the gardens at dusk. Pack repellent and keep the room closed with the AC on in the evening.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Makathanee Resort, Koh Mak

faq.q: Which beach is Makathanee Resort on, and how do you get there?
faq.a: Makathanee sits on Ao Kao Beach on the southern side of Koh Mak. Its standout feature is that the resort has its own pier — speedboats from Laem Ngop, Koh Chang and Koh Kood dock here, under 100 metres from the check-in desk. It's best to tell the resort in advance which pier you're coming from so they can arrange the boat/transfer.

faq.q: What does Makathanee Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,400/night with breakfast included for pool/sea-view and Deluxe rooms. There's a Honeymoon Suite with a jacuzzi (~฿1,700), a Panoramic Beach Bungalow (~฿1,800) and two-bedroom Family Suites (~฿2,700). Prices swing with the season — high and peak season cost more — so compare a few platforms before booking.

It's a strong choice for families and travellers who value convenience: the resort's pier is right out front, there are two pools, the shore shelves in gently for kids, and rooms come in many shapes and prices. It's not a luxury resort — it leans on value and a beachfront location rather than polish.

faq.q: Are the rooms dated? Which room should I request?
faq.a: Some reviews mention older buildings and bungalows that feel run down, with cleanliness not always consistent. We'd suggest asking for a renovated room in the hotel block, or the Deluxe/Suite tier, to get a room in better condition than the first-generation bungalows.

faq.q: Is Koh Mak open year-round, and when should I go?
faq.a: The best window is high season, October–May, when the sea is clear and calm. In low season (Jun–mid-Oct) there's rain and swell, and many places on the island close → if you're going off-season, confirm with the resort that it's open and that boats are running before you book.
